title: Record where a reflection came from
action: Implement docs/history/trust-layers/CONTEXT.md D3 (the verb half) as refined by D6, and contract C2. Anchors in verbs/mailbox.rs: `pub(crate) const FIX_AT_VALUES: [&str; 4] = ["architecture", "check", "doctrine", "none"];`, the function `read_reflection` holding `let missing: Vec<&str> = [("--wrong", wrong), ("--better", better), ("--fix-at", fix_at)]`, `pub(crate) fn reflection(at: &str, wrong: &str, better: &str, fix_at: &str) -> Self {`, the structs `Entry` and `LetterItem` with their `to_value`, and the frontmatter writer that uses `emit_opt`; in verbs/mailbox_digest.rs: `fn reflection_key(fix_at: Option<&str>, what: &str) -> Option<String> {`. Add an optional --source flag to bee mailbox reflect with the closed, lower-case, exact set self, user, review; default self. Shape: an optional source field on Entry and on LetterItem (the entry must hold every fact the letter prints). Entry and LetterItem are built by struct literals in other places too: `let entry = mailbox::Entry {` in verbs/cells/handlers_close.rs (two sites) and verbs/drivers/close.rs, and `Entry {` in a test helper in verbs/work.rs; give each of those sites an absent source and change nothing else there. Absent or self: the stored entry row carries no source key, and the letter item carries none, so both are byte-identical to before this change (the serializers must insert the key only when it is set, never as null). user or review: the entry row and the letter item carry source with that word, and the Mistakes & reflection bullet for that entry says `your correction` for user and `from a review` for review. Any other value, an empty value included: exit non-zero, append nothing, and name the three legal values in the error. --source together with --no-mistakes: refused, the same way --wrong with --no-mistakes is. The --json result of the verb carries source when it is set. A reflection read back from a cap trace has no source. reflection_key must not read source: two reflections with the same layer and the same first four words fold into one key whatever their sources. An entry read back with no source key is a self reflection. Register --source on the mailbox reflect verb in generated/registry_payload.json with a description of the three values, so bee mailbox reflect --help lists it and the CLI-shape guard accepts it. That file is one compact JSON line and is hand-edited: change it by a JSON round-trip that keeps its compact byte format and key order. The flag name source already exists in the registry vocabulary, so the pinned distinct-flag count in catalog.rs must not change; if a test says it does, stop and report. Do not change the --mistake path of bee cells cap beyond the absent source. Red first, with test names that contain reflect_source: a default call stores no source key and its letter item has none; user and review are stored and rendered with the two phrases; an off-set value and an empty value refuse and append nothing; --source with --no-mistakes refuses; a user reflection and a self reflection with the same layer and what produce the same lesson key. No code comments. The proof run must show the new tests ran: quote the count of tests the filter matched, which must be above zero.
verify: cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml --bin bee -- reflect_source && cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml --test registry_contracts

The lesson key of a reflection does not depend on its source
